claims.text: The trip record establishes the two distances the POL-RD-01 threshold test runs on: the platform's booked optimal route was 14.0 km and the trip as driven was 18.2 km, an excess of 4.2 km. That excess is 30.0% of the optimal distance, so it clears the 20% limb of POL-RD-01, and it is 4.2 km in absolute terms, so it clears the 0.8 km limb as well. Both establishment tests pass and the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The governing distance figure is the trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record. POL-RD-01 says gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two disagree, and here the trace records 18.2 km against a booked optimal of 14.0 km, so the excess of 4.2 km is measured on the trace. The trace is impaired at schema level (GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, weight 0.6) and I disclose that, but the impairment does not change the distance finding: the single 100.0 s gap is one stretch of the run, and the excess is measured across the whole trip, not across the gap.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'Navigation rerouted me.' That is a general assertion of an external cause, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge the driver's burden. No advisory is on file for this trip at all: the traffic advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0, so there is nothing to compare the assertion against and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. The assertion carries no weight.

The missing advisory does not escalate this case. The driver named no evidence ID for any advisory, so the absent artifact is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5); it is a gap in the bundle. POL-RD-13(1) states that priority expressly, and POL-RD-13(2) provides that where the rider has shown an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour can be run on this record. The chat log carries zero messages, so there is no rider instruction, no timestamp and no waypoint_hint to test against the trace. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on the record and the excess is not reduced by it.

No relocation clause applies. The trip record shows original_pickup, original_dropoff, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null, and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no amended optimal substitutes for the booked 14.0 km. The booked optimal stands as the baseline.

The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs and the refund is arithmetic. The recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 19.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 20.42. The rider was charged 26.73. The refund is 26.73 - 20.42 = 6.31, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 6.35. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The rider is not carrying the disputed charge after this ruling. The fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the 6.35 refund moves money back to the filing rider and leaves the rider paying only the optimal-route fare.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due. The fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls and zero airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a charged gantry, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and nothing is double-counted.

The driver's repeat-deviation profile does not support an uplift. POL-RD-06 requires driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 3 or more, or a ratio of 0.05 or more against completed_trips_90d of at least 40. The burden has shifted to the driver, who has pointed to no artifact and no clause that exonerates the excess.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: on the arithmetic you are in the same place, and I agree with the numbers both briefs put forward. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02826), so the optimal-route recomputation is ((SGD 3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 km + 0.28 x 19.0 min) x 1.0 surge) + SGD 0.80 platform fee + SGD 0.00 ERP = SGD 20.42. Against the SGD 26.73 charged, the refund would be SGD 6.31, rounded up to SGD 6.35 - above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% full-refund share, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.35. I cannot issue that refund. The case escalates instead, the SGD 11.00 contested is held rather than collected or refunded, and no money moves now.

Why. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02826 is impaired at schema level - weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW - and it is impaired for POLICY purposes as well: the 100.0 second gap between fixes from 19:39:44 to 19:41:24, 1.01 km apart in a straight line, exceeds the 90-second limb of POL-RD-07(a). Both statements are true and I record both; the finding does not survive the discount, because everything the deviation rests on comes from that same trace.

Under POL-RD-07(ii) a deviation may not be established on an impaired trace alone and must be corroborated by an independent source. None of the listed kinds exists here. The chat log is empty (0 messages), so there is no driver admission there. The fare breakdown charges no ERP gantry, so no corridor is evidenced. The trip record's actual_distance_km of 18.2 km is, by POL-RD-01's own words, a rounded convenience copy of the trace measurement. The fare breakdown's distance_charged_km of 18.2 km is the same figure read off the same METERED trace - POL-RD-07(ii) says a billed distance that copies the trace figure is not independent, and this one copies it exactly. The driver's only explanation, 'Navigation rerouted me.', names no route and cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight; with no advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-02826-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) POL-RD-03 cannot be run. That absence does not itself escalate (POL-RD-13(1)), but it leaves the explanation weightless. The driver's brief argued the billed distance is independent corroboration; I reject that, for the reason just given.

Two escalation triggers fire. POL-RD-10(3): the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists. Independently, POL-RD-10(1): the fact the ruling would rest on - the distance actually driven - is carried only by the 0.6-weight trace (the trip record and the fare breakdown are copies of the same measurement, not independent carriers of it), so my confidence is capped at 0.6, below the 0.70 floor. To both parties: this is a hold, not a decision on the merits. The case goes to a human reviewer, no money moves, and the disputed SGD 11.00 is held rather than collected or refunded. Here is why, and what would settle it.

What the record shows. Trip TRP-02826 ran on 17 Aug 2026 from Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd to Blk 420 Woodlands St 41. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02826, weight 1.0) books an optimal route of 14.0 km and 19.0 minutes; the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02826, weight 1.0) shows a METERED fare charged at SGD 26.73, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02826) records 18.2 km. Measured against the booked optimal, that is an excess of 4.2 km (30.0%), above both POL-RD-01 tests (20% and 0.8 km).

The evidence that measures it is impaired, twice over. The admissibility pre-pass tags EV-GPS-02826 IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW; and it also meets this policy's own, looser limb POL-RD-07(a), because it contains a 100.0-second gap between consecutive fixes (19:39:44 to 19:41:24), more than the 90 seconds that clause allows. Both findings are stated, as POL-RD-07 requires.

Because the trace is impaired for policy purposes, POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing the deviation on the trace alone; a source from that clause's list is required. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02826, weight 1.0) holds zero messages, so there is no driver admission in chat. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry line placing the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. And the two other distance figures - trip_record.actual_distance_km and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km, both 18.2 km - are copies of the same trace measurement (POL-RD-01 says the trip record figure is a rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test; POL-RD-07(ii) says the billed distance is not independent where it copies the trace). That is one measurement in three places, not three. The driver's statement, 'Navigation rerouted me', is an assertion of an external cause: POL-RD-13 tests it against the traffic advisory and nothing else, and no advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-02826-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and supplies no independent measurement of the route; read at its highest as a bare concession that a reroute happened, it is still not a weighted artifact and cannot lift the confidence cap below.

Confidence. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence is capped by the artifact carrying the deciding fact - here the distance actually driven, and with it the excess. That fact rests on EV-GPS-02826 at weight 0.6 and on nothing independent of it. The counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier and enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the cap. My confidence therefore cannot exceed 0.6, below the policy's 0.70 floor.

The triggers. Two grounds in POL-RD-10 are engaged, and each alone is terminal. POL-RD-10(3): the GPS trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists on this record. POL-RD-10(1): independently, my confidence cannot reach the 0.70 floor because the deciding fact rests on an artifact at weight 0.6. ESCALATE replaces the ruling; both monetary fields are null; the disputed amount is held.

What would resolve it. A re-exported GPS trace without the 100.0-second sampling gap, or an independent record of the route - a driver admission in the chat log, an ERP gantry record placing the vehicle on the longer corridor, or a trip-record driven distance the platform derived independently of this trace. Any of those would let the deviation be established, and if the carrier were at weight 0.70 or more a monetary ruling could issue.

The money, if it could issue. Had the deviation been provable, POL-RD-02 on the booked optimal route would give ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 19.0) x the 1.0 surge read from EV-FARE-02826) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.42, and the refund would be 26.73 - 20.42 = 6.35, above the 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share. Both advocates reached that figure and their arithmetic is correct; it cannot be paid out because the finding it rests on is not safe.

The advocates' other claims are accepted and change nothing: no rider-requested detour (chat log empty - POL-RD-04, R2/D1); no pickup or dropoff relocation (POL-RD-05, R3/D2); not a pooled trip (RYDE_X, so the 14.0 km solo optimal is the right comparator - POL-RD-12, D3); the fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route (D4); no ERP, toll or surcharge correction is due (zero lines, no airport surcharge - POL-RD-09, R6/D9); no repeat-deviation pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 287 - POL-RD-06, R7/D7); and the rider's profile does not trigger extra corroboration (deviation_claims_60d 0 - POL-RD-08, R8/D8). R1's suggestion that the 100-second gap is 'one stretch' and does not affect the distance finding is rejected: POL-RD-07 does not read the impairment that way, and once the trace is impaired the deviation needs a source outside it. D6's assertion that the fare breakdown's distance_charged_km is independently derived is rejected for the reason given above. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter mentioned by both sides is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used to decide anything. No referral fires: there is no POL-RD-06(c) conduct pattern to refer and no POL-RD-09(4) phantom charge line to correct.
